sections.h2: What does the Washtenaw County Register of Deeds handle?
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds keeps the real and personal property records for land in Washtenaw County, including deeds, mortgages and foreclosure records. It sits under the county's Clerk / Register of Deeds department, and every recorded document is open to the public.

The county's Register of Deeds page links to separate pages for document recording and requirements, searching and requesting records, eRecording, the fee schedule and the Michigan transfer tax. It also offers an online land record search where copies can be bought, and a login is required for that purchase.

For a seller, the practical point is simple. Your deed is not final for the public until it is recorded here, and most closings send it through a title company. Ask that company for the recording date and for the recorded copy once the county has processed it.

sections.h2: How can you record a Washtenaw County deed electronically?
sections.html:
The county accepts eRecording through vendors that the Register of Deeds has approved, so title agents and lenders can submit papers without a trip to Ann Arbor. The county's eRecording page describes it as electronic submission through an approved vendor.

An individual seller who signs a deed outside a title closing usually records on paper, by mail or at the counter. Check the document recording page before you send anything, because a paper that misses the layout rules is returned.

  • Confirm the current fee on the county's fee schedule page, which covers recording, copies, searches, transfer tax and tax certificates.
  • Ask whether the office takes checks, cards or only specific payment types for your filing.
  • Keep the original signed deed safe until the county has accepted it for recording.

sections.h2: What fees and tax rates apply to a Washtenaw County deed?
sections.html:
State law sets the baseline charges for a register of deeds, and Washtenaw's fee schedule page is where the county confirms the amount for each service. The table lists the statutory figures and the two transfer tax rates.

Michigan recording charges and transfer tax rates that frame a Washtenaw County filing
ChargeAmount in statuteSource
Entering and recording a document$30.00 regardless of pagesMCL 600.2567(1)(a)
Each extra instrument assigned or discharged$3.00MCL 600.2567(1)(b)
Copies of records$1.00 per pageMCL 600.2567(1)(c)
Certifying a recorded document$5.00MCL 600.2567(1)(d)
County transfer tax55 cents per $500 or fraction (county under 2,000,000 people)MCL 207.504
State transfer tax$3.75 per $500 or fractionMCL 207.525

The statute is posted on the Michigan Legislature site. Order copies of your own recorded deed before listing the house, so you have the legal description and recording details ready for the buyer's title company.

sections.h2: Who owes the transfer tax on a Washtenaw County sale, and who is exempt?
sections.html:
The seller owes it. Under MCL 207.523, the person selling or granting the property is liable, and payment goes to the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed is delivered to the buyer. Washtenaw's transfer tax page adds that the tax is collected unless the deed is exempt and the exemption is stated on the face of the deed.

That last point matters. If you rely on an exemption, the reason has to appear on the deed itself. MCL 207.526 lists the exemptions, including:

  • A conveyance from a spouse or couple that creates or ends a tenancy by the entireties.
  • A transfer from an individual to a child, stepchild, adopted child or grandchild.
  • A boundary line adjustment with no money changing hands.
  • A joint tenancy created when at least one of the owners already holds the property.
  • A deed given in a mortgage foreclosure or in lieu of one.

Someone who paid and later finds the sale was exempt can ask the state Treasury department for a refund under MCL 207.523(4).

sections.h2: Does a Washtenaw County deed need a tax certificate?
sections.html:
Often, yes. MCL 211.135 tells every register of deeds to ask for county treasurer certificates before recording a deed or land contract. The certificates state whether tax liens or tax titles exist and confirm that all taxes were paid for the five years before the date of the instrument.

The statute excuses quitclaim deeds and other conveyances with no covenants of warranty, along with sheriff's deeds and a few other categories. A warranty deed from a Washtenaw County seller therefore normally needs the certificate first.

If taxes are behind, the Washtenaw County Treasurer is the office to ask for a payoff figure. Settle that balance at or before closing so the certificate can issue and the deed can be recorded without delay.

sections.h2: How should a deed be prepared for Washtenaw County recording?
sections.html:
Layout rules come from MCL 565.201, and a register of deeds cannot accept a paper that breaks them. Check each item before signing day.

  • The first printed line on page one names a single recordable event, such as a warranty deed.
  • Black ink on white paper of at least 20-pound weight, in 10-point type or larger.
  • At least 2 1/2 inches of clear space at the top of page one and 1/2 inch on the other sides.
  • Grantee addresses on every deed, and the drafter's name and business address.
  • No more than the last four digits of a Social Security number visible.
  • An English translation attached when any part is in another language.

The Register of Deeds also offers Fraud Guard alerts, a sign-up that tells you when a document is recorded under your name, which is a useful safeguard while a house is on the market or sitting vacant. Two other county pages help sellers with older paperwork. One explains how to discharge prohibited deed restrictions, such as covenants that discriminate by race or religion. The other describes the Michigan Construction Lien Act, which matters if contractors worked on the house recently.

sections.h2: What is Washtenaw County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Washtenaw County covers 722 square miles, of which 706 is land, and Ann Arbor is both the county seat and the largest city. Other cities are Chelsea, Dexter, Manchester, Saline, Ypsilanti and the northern part of Milan, and the county also has the village of Barton Hills and the Whitmore Lake community. Highways include I-94, US 23, US 12, M-14, M-17 and M-52.

The University of Michigan is the county's largest employer, followed by Trinity Health, federal government jobs, Ann Arbor Public Schools and the Toyota Technical Center, according to a July 2020 employer list. Eastern Michigan University is in Ypsilanti, and Washtenaw Community College and Concordia University Ann Arbor are also in the county.

The Census Bureau estimates 370,214 residents for 2025 and 165,103 housing units. Owners occupy 61.6 percent of homes, the median owner-occupied value is $374,100, median household income is $89,180 and median gross rent is $1,463. About 58.7 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree or more. Michigan assigns zoning, permits and assessing to cities and townships, so a permit question goes to the local unit rather than to the Register of Deeds.

faqs.q: Does Washtenaw County accept electronic recording of deeds?
faqs.a: Yes. The county takes documents for recording through eRecording vendors approved by the Register of Deeds. Title companies and lenders most often use that route.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax on a Washtenaw County sale?
faqs.a: The seller does. Michigan law makes the grantor liable and sets the combined rate at 55 cents plus $3.75 per $500 of value, with payment due to the county treasurer within 15 days of delivering the deed.

faqs.q: Do I need to state a transfer tax exemption on my Washtenaw County deed?
faqs.a: Yes. The county's transfer tax page says the tax is collected unless the instrument is exempt and the exemption is stated on the face of the deed. Spell out the statutory reason before you sign.

faqs.q: What tax proof does a Washtenaw County warranty deed need?
faqs.a: Certificates from the county treasurer showing no tax liens or titles and that taxes were paid for the preceding five years. Quitclaim deeds with no warranty covenants are excused from this step.

faqs.q: Where do I find the current Washtenaw County recording fee?
faqs.a: On the Register of Deeds fee schedule page, which lists recording, copies, searches, transfer tax and tax certificates. State law sets the baseline recording charge at $30.00 per document.
